This document holds the full parameter sweeps, the complete grids searched for each prior method, per-country scores, and timings in every density bin.
Every number comes from the same runs as the letter, scored against the released vector parcels.

\section{Full Parameter Sweeps}
Table~\ref{tab:supp_sweep} gives macro PQ for every setting of $\tau$ and $h$ on all four model and sensor pairs, and repeats the foreground and split-rule comparison for each of them.
The letter reports the two PlanetScope B3 and Sentinel-2 B7 columns.
The support threshold is flat between 0.7 and 0.9 on every pair, and $h=8$ loses accuracy on every pair because the $h$-maxima of small parcels disappear.

\section{Timing by Parcel Density}
Table~\ref{tab:supp_timing} gives the median milliseconds per patch in four density bins on both sensors, measured on one core with threads pinned, taking the fastest of three repeats after a warm-up call.
Thirty patches were sampled per bin with a fixed seed.
Sentinel-2 patches carry more pixels, so every method costs more there, and the ordering between methods does not change.

\section{Reproduction}
Predictions are cached once per checkpoint with the released inference settings, and every post-processing method reads that cache, so the comparison is not affected by inference differences.
The steps are: cache the softmax output of each released checkpoint; build the candidate polygon sets; score every method against the reference parcels; and generate the tables and figures.
Our implementation of the released conversion reproduces the published per-country panoptic quality for PlanetScope to within $10^{-3}$, and the same for Sentinel-2 under the native-resolution scoring of that paper.
